title: In the Theatre I

image.credit: collection not stated on source page; via arthistoryproject.com

altText: A painting titled In the Theatre I, showing a scene in a theater or similar public gathering place, with figures and large areas of strong, flat color rather than fine realistic detail.

context: A painting in tempera and gouache by Marianne von Werefkin, made in 1906. The page text names no collection and tags it with cafes, which may not match the title.

descriptions.k: This painting shows a place where people gather, like a theater. The colors are strong and the shapes are simple. Look at all the colors. Which one do you notice first? What would you hear there?
descriptions.g12: Marianne von Werefkin painted a scene in a theater. She used strong colors and big, simple shapes instead of tiny details. The paint looks flat, a bit like a poster. Which colors stand out? What mood do they make you feel?
descriptions.g35: Marianne von Werefkin painted In the Theatre I in 1906 using tempera and gouache, which are paints that dry matte and look flat and bold. She worked in the Expressionist style, using color to show feeling rather than copy reality. Which colors do you notice first, and what mood do they give the scene?
descriptions.g68: Werefkin's In the Theatre I (1906) is an Expressionist painting in tempera and gouache. These water-based, matte paints help produce flat, bold areas of color. Expressionist artists used color and simplified shape to express mood, not to copy nature. How do the colors and forms make a public place feel atmospheric, and what do they leave out? Use color and shape as evidence.
descriptions.g910: In the Theatre I (1906) is an Expressionist work in tempera and gouache. The medium encourages flat, saturated areas of color, and Werefkin uses them to convey a mood of a public setting rather than a detailed record. Expressionism prioritized feeling over naturalism. How do color, shape and cropping shape your sense of the scene, and what interpretations remain open? Look closely at the color boundaries and the figures.
descriptions.g1112: Werefkin's In the Theatre I (1906) uses tempera and gouache to produce flat, intense areas of color, a choice consistent with Expressionist interest in mood over description. Werefkin, a woman artist active in early modern circles, has often been less visible than her male contemporaries. How does the painting use color and simplification to suggest atmosphere, and what role does an artist's reputation play in how we look? Weigh the evidence in the colors, the shapes and the missing details.

teacherNote.context: A painting in tempera and gouache made in 1906 by Marianne von Werefkin, an Expressionist artist. The source page names no collection, so this entry does not state one.
directions: Have students paint a crowded place using only flat areas of color with no outlines, then discuss the mood created.
Ask students to compare matte paint and glossy paint and say which suits a theater scene better.
Discuss why some artists' work is better known than others and how teachers and students can look at lesser-known artists.
